newsitem.title: USA: Famed Impressionist collection to be sold.
newsitem.headline: Famed Impressionist collection to be sold.

text.p: One of the last great private collections of Impressionist art will be sold at auction in May, with rare portraits by Manet and Cezanne expected to fetch more than $25 million each, Christie's auction house said on Wednesday.

The collection, which belonged to John and Frances Loeb, is being sold by the late couple's children to set up a new philanthropic organisation to support programmes in education, health, family planning and the arts.

Christie's chairman Christopher Burge said the Loeb collection of 30 paintings, which will be sold in New York on May 12, could fetch more than $80 million. He called it one of the last great Impressionist collections still in private hands.

The collection includes a rare self-portrait by Edouard Manet, one of only three self-portraits that he is believed to have done, and a rare portrait by Cezanne of his wife, one of four that the artist did and the last still in private hands.
Both paintings are expected to fetch more than $25 million, Burge said.

The German critic Wilhelm Haulstein called the portrait of Madame Cezanne one of "the most extraordinary works of modern painting. To many painters and others interested in art, this picture is the goal for pilgrims."

Also to be offered for sale is a Cezanne landscape, "Les Toits de L'Estaque," which is expected to sell for about $10 million, and a work on cardboard by Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec of a young dancer, which is expected to sell for about the same amount.

The Loebs built their collection in the 1950s and 60s. He was a pillar of Wall Street and headed Loeb, Rhoades & Company for many years. His wife Frances was New York City's commissioner for the United Nations for 12 years and was a niece of former New York Senator and Governor Herbert Lehman.
